subject: Re: Deployment mode qualification — Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)
messages:

Cc: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap: deployment mode needs (Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Thanks again for the call earlier, Aisha and Tom — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we're aligned on the data isolation qualification you requested.

Summary of your requirements (as I understand them):
- Production workloads will process customer PII and regulatory data (PCI + regulated financial PII).
- You need verifiable network isolation and customer-controlled encryption keys for production data.
- SOC 2 evidence (audit logs, retention policy) will be required for procurement.
- Minimum tolerance for cross-tenant data exposure; preference toward no shared tenancy in prod.

How Redwood options map to those requirements: 
- Hosted API (public): fastest to start but does not meet your requirement for customer-managed networking or KMS; data-in-transit encryption and contractual protections are available, but there is shared multi-tenant compute. Not recommended for this use case.
- Dedicated capacity: provides reserved compute pools (single-tenant GPU pools), configurable retention and stronger logical isolation. You retain control over who can access your capacity within Redwood, and we can restrict model variants and routing. However, networking still routes through Redwood-managed infrastructure — we can provide strict ACLs and private peering options, but full VPC isolation (no shared control plane egress) is not native in hosted Dedicated.
- Private VPC / on-prem: provides the strongest isolation. With Private VPC we deploy a customer-dedicated control plane (or an on-prem package) in your VPC, integrate with your KMS/HSM for keys, and you control network egress. This meets the requirement for customer-controlled keys and minimizes cross-tenant exposure.

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) I'll send a short Q&A covering SOC2 evidence points and network/KMS options (will attach).
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Mateo (solutions engineer) to walk through the Private VPC architecture and runbook.
3) If Private VPC looks good, we'll produce a targeted estimate and procurement checklist (DocuSign + SOW).

Can you confirm the list above reflects your needs and whether you have a hard requirement for customer-managed KMS (vs Redwood-managed keys with BYOK rotation)?

Best,
– Marissa

Thanks, Marissa — that summary is helpful and mostly accurate. A couple clarifying items from our security/compliance side: 

1) KMS: firm requirement for customer-managed keys (we need control and auditability via our KMS/HSM). Redwood-managed key custody will be a blocker for production.
2) Network isolation: we need the option to run in our VPC with no outbound internet egress from model hosts (other than controlled update channels). Is Private VPC able to support a fully air-gapped/on-prem model?
3) Audit logs: we need token-level request logs, model versioning history, and retention settings configurable to 7 years for audit purposes. Is that feasible?

Also — timeline question: we are targeting a pilot environment for limited workloads in Q3, with production in Q4 if procurement clears.

Can Mateo join a technical call next week? Prefer Tue/Wed morning PT.

Appreciate the attach — I'll review.

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: deployment mode needs (Dedicated vs Private VPC)

Great questions — answer below and added attachments (Q&A + a sketch of the Private VPC architecture).

KMS: Yes — Private VPC deployments support full integration with customer-managed KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault with HSM, or on-prem HSM). We can configure encryption-at-rest such that keys are never in Redwood KMS. That satisfies the customer-managed-keys requirement.

Network isolation / air-gapped: We support two Private deployment patterns:
- Private VPC (managed control plane + data plane in your VPC): model hosts run in your VPC with no public IPs; all egress can be restricted via your network controls. The control plane can be configured to be reachable only over a management VPN or private peering.
- On-prem package (air-gapped): for highly regulated customers we can deliver an on-prem install where updates are managed via scheduled, signed bundles; no persistent outbound egress required.

Audit logs & retention: We emit request-level logs (request id, model version, prompt hashes, timestamps) and control-plane audit logs (config changes, user access). Retention windows are configurable; 7-year retention can be supported via integration with your logging/SIEM (we can stream logs to your AWS S3/CloudWatch/Log Analytics with lifecycle rules for long-term retention).

Pilot timeline: Q3 pilot is realistic. Typical Private VPC onboarding (network setup, KMS integration, security review) takes 4–8 weeks depending on procurement and network approvals. We'll prioritize the pilot path if we lock scope this quarter.

Proposed next steps:
- Mateo to run a 60-minute technical deep-dive next Tue (2027-05-25) 10:00–11:00 PT. Mateo — are you available?
- I'll open a HubSpot RFP record and share the procurement checklist (DocuSign + SOW) once we agree on pilot scope.

Attachments included: FinSecure_Audit_Q&A.xlsx; redwood-private-vpc-arch.pdf

Best,
– Marissa
